findings.source_fact: All three install methods require no existing profile and each installs its own bound profile method.
findings.consequence: Calling the existing install methods sequentially cannot yield three installed observers. A replacing dispatcher also fails their bound-method identity checks.

findings.source_fact: Bridge audit refuses additional sys.addaudithook/sys.setprofile, and profile refuses native os.register_at_fork c_call.
findings.consequence: The bridge does not grant a registration observer an exception merely because its callback arguments are bound.

findings.source_fact: Native guard audit permits writing only at the exact package lock and refuses link/remove/rmdir; its mkdir route accepts only an existing package-lock parent.
findings.consequence: Scratch permission from another hook cannot undo the native hook refusal.

findings.source_fact: Registration audit refuses writes, filesystem mutations and fcntl routes.
findings.consequence: A second observer allowing scratch or package-lock operations cannot make the stack accept them.

findings.source_fact: Native guard check compares effective and kernel environments to its fixed fourteen-field environment() dictionary.
findings.consequence: The declared TMPDIR field must use a separate implementation; injecting this contract into the closed guard would refuse.

findings.source_fact: Registration binder only accepts FunctionType with no closure or positional defaults; original wrapper inventory has audit/fork/exit only.
findings.consequence: Bound Python/class/native lock methods, logging defaults, Random.seed closure and threading._register_atexit partial/list lifecycle need separate exact bindings.

findings.source_fact: FilelockScratch.run installs an audit hook and directly calls its supplied capability callback.
findings.consequence: The composed real import route must observe import-triggered entry/return; it must not invoke run() to replay that callback.

findings.source_fact: The saved v2 probe exception/finally paths set guard.active=False and sys.setprofile(None), then use normal sys.exit on failure.
findings.consequence: Do not reuse that failure epilogue for a callback-bearing import. The prospective route keeps observers and uses a bounded diagnostic capability followed by os._exit, with all partial evidence retained. This is a future requirement, not a claim about old callback execution.
